# dataversecontact_table (Resource)

Manages a table schema in the Dataverse Contact API. The schema is saved as a draft and immediately published.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A citizen-owned table: cases raised by the signed-in citizen.
resource "dataversecontact_table" "case" {
  scope       = "default"
  route_name  = "case"
  description = "Citizen service cases"

  dataverse_table = "incidents" # OData entity set name
  # dataverse_logical_name omitted -> derived by singularizing: "incident"
  # required_permission omitted    -> defaults to route_name: "case"
  # filters omitted                -> defaults to ["statecode eq 0"]
  primary_key = "incidentid"

  default_select = ["title", "ticketnumber", "createdon", "statuscode"]
  lookup_fields  = ["title", "ticketnumber"]

  # Log the case number with every request that touches a case (or a note,
  # document or action on it), so App Insights can be searched for the number
  # a citizen quotes. Must be one of the fields below.
  reference = "ticketnumber"

  fields = {
    title = {
      type        = "string"
      description = "Case title."
    }
    ticketnumber = {
      type        = "string"
      description = "Case reference shown to the citizen."
      read_only   = true
    }
    createdon = {
      type        = "datetime"
      description = "When the case was raised."
      read_only   = true
    }
    new_iscomplex = {
      type        = "boolean"
      description = "Complex-case flag."
    }
    new_estimatedcost = {
      type        = "number"
      description = "Estimated cost."
    }
    statuscode = {
      type        = "choice"
      description = "Case status."
    }
    customerid = {
      type         = "lookup"
      description  = "The citizen this case belongs to."
      lookup_table = "contact"            # route name of the target table
      value_field  = "_customerid_value"  # polymorphic lookup's raw value column
      bind_field   = "customerid_contact" # navigation property for @odata.bind
    }
  }

  # How /me row-scoping walks from this table back to the caller's contact.
  contact_join_step {
    table = "contacts"
    from  = "customerid_contact"
    key   = "contactid"
  }

  # Return a couple of contact fields inline when the client expands the lookup.
  expand {
    lookup_field  = "customerid_contact"
    related_table = "contacts"

    field {
      name        = "fullname"
      type        = "string"
      description = "Citizen name."
    }
    field {
      name        = "emailaddress1"
      type        = "string"
      description = "Citizen email."
    }
  }

  # Bind the citizen automatically on create, so a caller can only ever
  # create cases owned by themselves.
  create_default {
    field      = "customerid_contact"
    bind_to    = "contact"
    entity_set = "contacts"
  }

  # The SharePoint documents in each case's folder, listed with
  # GET /me/case/{id}/documents and uploaded through
  # POST /me/case/{id}/documents/uploads. Both need `casedocuments`, granted in
  # dataversecontact_permissions_sync like a route: "me" lists, "create" uploads.
  #   default_permissions = { case = ["me", "write", "create"], casedocuments = ["me", "create"] }
  # Reading the case isn't enough on its own. Only documents an officer has
  # marked ShowOnPortal in the library are listed.
  documents {
    permission = "casedocuments"
    columns    = { ShowOnPortal = "boolean" } # SharePoint internal name = type
    filters    = ["ShowOnPortal eq true"]
    # folder   = "Public"                    # serve a sub-folder instead

    # Leave upload out to allow no uploads. Every uploaded file is marked
    # ShowOnPortal, so the citizen sees what they sent.
    upload {
      columns = { ShowOnPortal = "true" } # fixed: callers can't change it
      # max_bytes  = 5242880              # default 10 MiB, never above the deployment's cap
      # extensions = ["pdf", "jpg", "png"] # default: common documents and images
    }
  }
}

# A public catalog table: readable without authentication, no citizen owner.
resource "dataversecontact_table" "service" {
  scope           = "default"
  route_name      = "service"
  description     = "Service categories citizens browse"
  dataverse_table = "bookableresourcecategories"
  primary_key     = "bookableresourcecategoryid"
  public_read     = true

  aliases = ["services", "category", "categories"]

  default_select = ["bookableresourcecategoryid", "name", "description"]
  lookup_fields  = ["name"]

  fields = {
    bookableresourcecategoryid = {
      type        = "string"
      description = "Unique service identifier."
      read_only   = true
    }
    name = {
      type        = "string"
      description = "Service name."
    }
    description = {
      type        = "string"
      description = "Service description."
    }
  }
}

# A polymorphic family: publish every target of a lookup as a route, without
# declaring one dataversecontact_table per target.
#
# Service Builder emits one Dataverse table per service and points
# incident.sb_service_recordid at it, so the set grows whenever a service
# ships. Declaring the RULE means a new service is readable the moment its
# table exists — there is no generated table list to regenerate, and nothing
# to remember after a publish.
resource "dataversecontact_table" "case_with_service_answers" {
  scope                  = "fcc"
  route_name             = "case"
  dataverse_table        = "incidents"
  dataverse_logical_name = "incident"
  primary_key            = "incidentid"
  required_permission    = "case"

  default_select = ["incidentid", "title", "sb_service_recordid"]
  lookup_fields  = ["title"]

  fields = {
    title = { type = "string", description = "Case title." }
    # The rule's field must also be declared as a lookup here, or
    # ?expand=sb_service_recordid cannot be rewritten onto the concrete
    # targets — it fails by returning nothing, not by erroring.
    #
    # It deliberately carries NO lookup_table, and must not be given one: a
    # polymorphic lookup points at many tables, so naming one would be a claim
    # the data contradicts. Dataverse says which target a given row used, and
    # the API surfaces that as sb_service_recordid_logicalname. The provider
    # exempts a field named by polymorphic_lookup from the lookup_table rule
    # for exactly this reason.
    sb_service_recordid = {
      type        = "lookup"
      description = "Your submitted answers."
      read_only   = true
    }
  }

  # Derived routes inherit this, with the reverse hop into `incidents`
  # prefixed — so they need no join of their own.
  contact_join_step {
    table = "contacts"
    from  = "customerid_contact"
    key   = "contactid"
  }

  polymorphic_lookup {
    field               = "sb_service_recordid"
    required_permission = "servicerecord"
    route_prefix_strip  = "sb_" # sb_missed_bin → GET /me/missed_bin/{id}
    exclude_targets     = ["sb_service_request"]

    # Each service table has its own business process flow. With this, every
    # case row carries `progress` — the stage its service record is in — or
    # null. One extra Dataverse read per page, never one per row. For a
    # process on the table ITSELF, set `business_process` on the resource.
    business_process = { expose_as = "progress" }
  }
}

# One entry covers the whole family. The API fans `servicerecord` out onto
# every derived route, because default_permissions is keyed by ROUTE name and
# a key naming only the permission would match no table and grant nothing.
resource "dataversecontact_permissions_sync" "fcc" {
  scope = "fcc"

  default_permissions = {
    case          = ["me", "write", "create"]
    servicerecord = ["me"]
  }

  depends_on = [dataversecontact_table.case_with_service_answers]
}

# Emails the signed-in contact was on, with their attachments as files.
#
# The contact is reached through the email's activity parties (a reverse
# step), and `match` counts a party only as From, To, CC or BCC. Without it,
# the Regarding party Dataverse adds for the record an email is filed against
# would make an internal email "one the contact was on".
#
# Attachments are rows of activitymimeattachments. Callers list them with
# GET /me/emails/{id}/files and download one through a short-lived link from
# POST /me/emails/{id}/files/{fileId}/link; the content is never inline.
resource "dataversecontact_table" "emails" {
  scope                  = "default"
  route_name             = "emails"
  dataverse_table        = "emails"
  dataverse_logical_name = "email"
  primary_key            = "activityid"
  required_permission    = "emails"
  default_select         = ["activityid", "subject", "sender", "torecipients", "senton", "attachmentcount"]
  lookup_fields          = ["subject"]
  filters                = ["statecode eq 1"] # sent or received, never drafts

  contact_join_step {
    table   = "activityparties"
    from    = "email_activity_parties"
    key     = "activitypartyid"
    reverse = true
    match   = { participationtypemask = [1, 2, 3, 4] } # sender, to, cc, bcc
  }
  contact_join_step {
    table = "contacts"
    from  = "partyid_contact"
    key   = "contactid"
  }

  files = {
    table         = "activitymimeattachments"
    primary_key   = "activitymimeattachmentid"
    parent_column = "objectid"
    content       = "body"
    file_name     = "filename"
    mime_type     = "mimetype"
    size          = "filesize"
  }

  fields = {
    activityid      = { type = "string", description = "Email id", read_only = true }
    subject         = { type = "string", description = "Subject", read_only = true }
    description     = { type = "string", description = "Body (HTML; render it sanitised)", read_only = true }
    sender          = { type = "string", description = "From address", read_only = true }
    torecipients    = { type = "string", description = "To addresses", read_only = true }
    senton          = { type = "datetime", description = "Sent on", read_only = true }
    attachmentcount = { type = "number", description = "Number of attachments", read_only = true }
  }
}

# A note's own attachment: the row is the file, so only the columns are named.
# Its content column (documentbody) is removed from the table's fields.
#   files = { content = "documentbody", file_name = "filename", mime_type = "mimetype", size = "filesize" }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dataverse_table` (String) The Dataverse OData entity set name (e.g. "incidents").
- `default_select` (List of String) Default $select fields when client doesn't specify.
- `fields` (Attributes Map) Field definitions keyed by Dataverse logical name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--fields))
- `lookup_fields` (List of String) Fields returned by the /lookup route.
- `primary_key` (String) The primary key field name.
- `route_name` (String) The URL-friendly route name for this table (e.g. "case").
- `scope` (String) The scope this table belongs to (e.g. "default").

### Optional

- `aliases` (List of String) Optional route aliases.
- `alternate_contact_join_path` (Block List) Additional join paths to the contact (OR'd with contact_join_step). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--alternate_contact_join_path))
- `business_process` (Attributes) Expose this table's own business process flow on this table's rows. Every row then carries an object (`progress` unless expose_as renames it) with the process instance's state, active stage and ordered stages — or null when there is no process or no instance for the row. Derived by the API per request, read-only, not selectable. The API's Dataverse application user needs Read on workflow, processstage and the process's instance table. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--business_process))
- `contact_join_step` (Block List) Steps to join back to the contact from this table (ordered). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--contact_join_step))
- `create_default` (Block List) Lookup fields automatically bound when creating a record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--create_default))
- `dataverse_logical_name` (String) The Dataverse entity logical name (e.g. "incident"). If omitted, derived by singularizing dataverse_table.
- `description` (String) Human-readable description of this table.
- `documents` (Block, Optional) SharePoint documents in each row's folder. Dataverse's SharePoint integration keeps a folder per row; with this, GET /{tier}/{route}/{id}/documents lists what is in it (one folder level, read through Microsoft Graph). The row is checked with this table's own scoping first. Listing needs the documents permission at that tier, not this table's: grant it in dataversecontact_permissions_sync.default_permissions under the same name (e.g. casedocuments = ["me"]). Each document carries id, name, folder, isFolder, mimeType, size, createdon and modifiedon, plus the columns declared here. Switch document management on for the table in Dataverse, and grant the API's service principal Sites.Selected with Read on the site. Add an upload block to let callers upload files too. Needs Contact API 1.34.0 or later: an older API keeps the key without an error but serves no documents. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--documents))
- `expand` (Block List) Expandable lookup fields — one level deep into related tables. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--expand))
- `fetch_xml` (String) FetchXML template for custom list queries.
- `files` (Attributes) Downloadable files on this table's rows (a note's attachment, an email's attachments). Callers list them with GET /{tier}/{route}/{id}/files and get a short-lived download link with POST .../files/{fileId}/link; the content is never returned inline. Leave out table, primary_key and parent_column when the row is the file; set all three when the files are rows of a child table. A file on the row itself drops its content column from the table's fields. Needs Contact API 1.31.0 or later: an older API drops this key without an error. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--files))
- `filters` (List of String) Always-on filter expressions applied to every query. Defaults to ["statecode eq 0"].
- `icon` (String) Icon filename (e.g. "incident.svg").
- `invites` (List of String) What a one-time invite link may do on this table, for someone with no account: "create" (on a child table such as casenotes, add one row under its parent, e.g. a note on a case; on any other table, log one new row) and "update" (change named columns of one row, once). Sending one from the API needs invite plus create or write on this table at that tier (e.g. casenotes = ["invite", "create"]); officers can also send them from the Portal Access app. A contact table takes "update" only. Uploads are documents.upload.invites. Set the scope's invite_url on dataversecontact_permissions_sync so links point at the portal. Needs Contact API 1.37.0 or later.
- `lookup_search_contains` (List of String) Lookup fields that use 'contains' instead of 'startswith'.
- `parent_table` (Block, Optional) Parent table relationship for child record tables. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--parent_table))
- `permission_group` (String) Permission group name for shared permissions.
- `polymorphic_lookup` (Block, Optional) Publish every target of a polymorphic lookup on this table as a route of its own, derived by the API from live Dataverse metadata — instead of declaring one dataversecontact_table per target.

Scoping needs no declaring: a target row has no lookup back to the caller, so its path is the reverse hop into this table (read from metadata) followed by this table's own contact_join_step chain. Grant the whole family in one go by adding required_permission to dataversecontact_permissions_sync.default_permissions.

A target's columns are published without anyone reviewing them — that is the trade for never going stale. Fields are read-only by default; target_prefix and exclude_targets bound the family if the lookup reaches further than intended. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--polymorphic_lookup))
- `public_choices` (Boolean) Whether choice/option set values are publicly accessible. Defaults to true.
- `public_create` (Boolean) Whether unauthenticated POST is allowed on the public tier.
- `public_read` (Boolean) Whether this table is publicly readable without authentication.
- `reference` (String) The column people quote for a row, such as a case's "ticketnumber". Every request that touches a row of this table, or something attached to it (a note, a document upload, an action), logs the row's value as reference in App Insights, so a free-text search for the case number finds it. Must be one of fields, of type string or number. Needs Contact API 1.40.0 or later: an older API keeps the key without an error but logs nothing.
- `required_permission` (String) The base permission name (e.g. "case"). If omitted, defaults to route_name.
- `team_join_step` (Block List) Steps to join back to the account for team-scoped queries (ordered). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--team_join_step))

### Read-Only

- `field_count` (Number) Number of fields defined in the schema.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the format {scope}/{route_name}.
- `source` (String) The source of the published schema ("published", "built-in").

<a id="nestedatt--fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `fields`

Required:

- `description` (String) Human-readable field description.
- `type` (String) Field data type: "string", "number", "datetime", "boolean", "lookup" or "choice".

Optional:

- `bind_field` (String) For aliased fields: the navigation property for @odata.bind writes. If omitted, the API derives it from the lookup's navigation property. An API that reports derived values separately (Contact API with admin GET `derived`) keeps them out of state.
- `lookup_table` (String) For lookup fields: the route name of the target table.
- `read_only` (Boolean) If true, field is read-only (not writable via PATCH).
- `value_field` (String) For polymorphic lookups: the underlying OData value column name.


<a id="nestedblock--alternate_contact_join_path"></a>
### Nested Schema for `alternate_contact_join_path`

Optional:

- `step` (Block List) Steps in this alternate path (ordered). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--alternate_contact_join_path--step))

<a id="nestedblock--alternate_contact_join_path--step"></a>
### Nested Schema for `alternate_contact_join_path.step`

Required:

- `from` (String) Navigation property or lookup field to follow.
- `key` (String) Primary key field on the target table.
- `table` (String) Dataverse table name for this step.

Optional:

- `match` (Map of List of Number) Reverse steps only: conditions the related row must also meet, inside the same any() lambda — column logical name to the option-set values it may have, e.g. { participationtypemask = [1, 2, 3, 4] } so an email counts only when the contact is its sender or a recipient. Needs Contact API 1.31.0 or later: an older API drops match without an error and joins on every related row, which for emails includes the Regarding party.
- `reverse` (Boolean) If true, `from` is a collection-valued navigation property; this step compiles to an OData any() lambda that scopes an ownerless child through the parent that references it (e.g. booking via servicebooking).



<a id="nestedatt--business_process"></a>
### Nested Schema for `business_process`

Optional:

- `expose_as` (String) Property name on each row. Defaults to "progress". Must not collide with a field of this table.


<a id="nestedblock--contact_join_step"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contact_join_step`

Required:

- `from` (String) Navigation property or lookup field to follow.
- `key` (String) Primary key field on the target table.
- `table` (String) Dataverse table name for this step.

Optional:

- `match` (Map of List of Number) Reverse steps only: conditions the related row must also meet, inside the same any() lambda — column logical name to the option-set values it may have, e.g. { participationtypemask = [1, 2, 3, 4] } so an email counts only when the contact is its sender or a recipient. Needs Contact API 1.31.0 or later: an older API drops match without an error and joins on every related row, which for emails includes the Regarding party.
- `reverse` (Boolean) If true, `from` is a collection-valued navigation property; this step compiles to an OData any() lambda that scopes an ownerless child through the parent that references it (e.g. booking via servicebooking).


<a id="nestedblock--create_default"></a>
### Nested Schema for `create_default`

Required:

- `bind_to` (String) What to bind it to: "contact" or "account".
- `entity_set` (String) The Dataverse entity set for the @odata.bind URL.
- `field` (String) The navigation property / lookup field name.


<a id="nestedblock--documents"></a>
### Nested Schema for `documents`

Optional:

- `columns` (Map of String) SharePoint library columns to return and allow filtering on: internal name (e.g. "ShowOnPortal", "Doc_x0020_Type") to type, one of "string", "number", "datetime" or "boolean". At most 30.
- `filters` (List of String) Restrictions applied to every listing, in the API's filter syntax: one "field operator value" per entry (e.g. "ShowOnPortal eq true"), all ANDed, naming only document fields and declared columns. Not OData: no and/or, no functions. A caller's own filters narrow them and never widen them. At most 10.
- `folder` (String) Sub-folder of each row's folder to serve instead (e.g. "Public" or "Public/2026"). Leave it out to serve the row's folder itself.
- `permission` (String) Required in the block. Permission subject that lists the documents (e.g. "casedocuments"): casedocuments, casedocuments:team and casedocuments:all per tier. Its read grants list the documents; with an upload block, its create grants (casedocuments:create, :create:team, :create:all) upload them.
- `upload` (Block, Optional) Lets callers upload a file into a row's folder, in three steps: POST /{tier}/{route}/{id}/documents/uploads with the file's name, size and type returns a short-lived upload URL; the caller PUTs the bytes to it; POST .../documents/uploads/{uploadId}/complete files them in SharePoint. Leave the block out to allow no uploads; upload {} allows them with the API's defaults. Uploading needs create on the documents permission at that tier, granted in dataversecontact_permissions_sync.default_permissions (e.g. casedocuments = ["me", "create"]); create doesn't imply listing. The row is checked with this table's own scoping first. A file never overwrites another (SharePoint renames a clash), and a row with no folder yet gets one. Grant the API's service principal Sites.Selected with Write on the site, and its Dataverse app user Create on Document Location. The upload URL is in the API's downloads storage, as for file downloads, and the storage account needs a CORS rule allowing PUT from the portal. Needs Contact API 1.35.0 or later: an older API keeps the key without an error but accepts no uploads. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--documents--upload))

<a id="nestedblock--documents--upload"></a>
### Nested Schema for `documents.upload`

Optional:

- `columns` (Map of String) SharePoint column values set on every uploaded file, e.g. { ShowOnPortal = "true" } so an upload passes filters = ["ShowOnPortal eq true"]. Each column must be declared in documents.columns, with its value written as a string that suits the declared type: "true" or "false" for boolean, a number such as "4" for number; the provider sends each as its type. Callers can't set or override them, and if they can't be set the upload is undone.
- `extensions` (List of String) File extensions accepted, lower case without the dot (e.g. ["pdf", "png", "jpg"]), matched case-insensitively. Leave it out for the API's default list: pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, heic, txt, rtf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, csv, odt, ods. Executable types (exe, bat, cmd, com, js, msi, ps1, scr, vbs, sh, dll) are never accepted.
- `invites` (Boolean) Let an officer send a one-time invite link to upload one document to a row, for someone with no account (the invite tier: POST /invite/{route}/{id}/documents/uploads, then .../{uploadId}/complete). Sending one from the API needs invite and create on the documents permission at that tier (e.g. casedocuments = ["invite", "create"]); officers can also send them from the Portal Access app. Set the scope's invite_url on dataversecontact_permissions_sync so links point at the portal. Needs Contact API 1.37.0 or later.
- `max_bytes` (Number) Largest file accepted, in bytes. Leave it out for 10485760 (10 MiB). Uploads are also capped by the deployment's DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES (26214400 = 25 MiB by default), so a larger value only applies where the deployment raised that.

Required:

Optional:

<a id="nestedblock--polymorphic_lookup"></a>
### Nested Schema for `polymorphic_lookup`

Optional:

- `business_process` (Attributes) Expose each target's business process flow on this table's rows. Every row then carries an object (`progress` unless expose_as renames it) with the process instance's state, active stage and ordered stages — or null when there is no process or no instance for the row. Derived by the API per request, read-only, not selectable. The API's Dataverse application user needs Read on workflow, processstage and the process's instance table. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--polymorphic_lookup--business_process))
- `exclude_targets` (List of String) Logical names never published, however they match.
- `field` (String) The polymorphic lookup on this table whose targets become routes (e.g. "sb_service_recordid"). Must also be declared in `fields` as a lookup, or ?expand=<field> cannot be rewritten onto the concrete targets.
- `read_only` (Boolean) Mark every derived field read-only. Defaults to true — a rule that publishes tables nobody reviewed should not also open them for writing.
- `required_permission` (String) Permission subject every derived route requires (e.g. "servicerecord"). Use this same name as the key in default_permissions — the API fans it out onto each derived route, which is what makes one entry cover the whole family.
- `route_prefix_strip` (String) Prefix removed from a target's logical name to form its route name ("sb_" turns sb_missed_bin into the route missed_bin). Also bounds which single-target lookups are inlined as expands, unless target_prefix is set.
- `target_prefix` (String) Only publish targets whose logical name starts with this. Unset publishes every target the lookup reaches.

<a id="nestedatt--polymorphic_lookup--business_process"></a>
### Nested Schema for `polymorphic_lookup.business_process`

Optional:

- `expose_as` (String) Property name on each row. Defaults to "progress". Must not collide with a field of this table.



<a id="nestedblock--team_join_step"></a>
### Nested Schema for `team_join_step`

Required:

- `from` (String) Navigation property or lookup field to follow.
- `key` (String) Primary key field on the target table.
- `table` (String) Dataverse table name for this step.

Optional:

- `match` (Map of List of Number) Reverse steps only: conditions the related row must also meet, inside the same any() lambda — column logical name to the option-set values it may have, e.g. { participationtypemask = [1, 2, 3, 4] } so an email counts only when the contact is its sender or a recipient. Needs Contact API 1.31.0 or later: an older API drops match without an error and joins on every related row, which for emails includes the Regarding party.
- `reverse` (Boolean) If true, `from` is a collection-valued navigation property; this step compiles to an OData any() lambda that scopes an ownerless child through the parent that references it (e.g. booking via servicebooking).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import id is {scope}/{route_name}
terraform import dataversecontact_table.case default/case
```
